instructions_to_ai.role: You are the lead product architect and full-stack engineer for BMU Hub.
source_of_truth_order: Uploaded UX/UI design files in this project (visual + layout authority)
This JSON (behaviour, data, permissions, flows authority)
BMU Master Operating System (process authority — embedded in workflow below)
BMU Services & Packages Catalogue 2026 (pricing authority — embedded in catalogue_seed)
rules: Follow the uploaded UX/UI designs exactly. Do not redesign, restyle or add screens that are not in the design unless this JSON requires them; if a required screen has no design, build it using the same components and tokens and flag it.
Make targeted changes when asked to revise. Never regenerate unrelated parts.
Enforce every gate, permission and rule in this JSON in the backend, not only in the UI.
Never expose internal-only data (internal notes, QC results, costs, margins, staff below CM, other clients) to client roles.
Use the exact vocabulary in glossary for team UI; use the client_label equivalents in client UI.
When something is ambiguous, choose the option that keeps the MOS rule intact and list the assumption in a short ASSUMPTIONS section of your output.
expected_outputs: RBAC policy file generated from permissions in this JSON
State machine definitions for engagement, cycle, deliverable, task, request, invoice
Screen-by-screen implementation mapped to uploaded designs
Test cases for every gate, rule and permission

design_system.authority: Uploaded UX/UI design files override everything in this block.
principles: One green primary action per screen
Charcoal for navigation and status, ivory for surfaces
Square corners on UI components (devices excepted)
Five-segment gate track on every project/engagement
Home screens open on 'What needs you', sorted by deadline

Responsive to 360px; keyboard focus visible; reduced motion respected

product.scale_target: Architected to support BMU's growth toward ₹100 Cr revenue: multi-tenant, multi-branch, white-label ready.

rules: Roles are permission sets; a user may hold multiple roles (e.g. CM + Strategist).
Custom roles can be cloned from a base role in Admin Panel.
Role changes require a manager at least one rank higher.
Every privileged action is written to the audit log.
Clients never message or tag production staff; all client messages route to the CM (Client → CM → Team).

key_screens.hierarchy_tree: Drag-and-drop org chart (Branch → Department → Team → User). Shows reporting line, roles, load %, active clients. Reassigning a manager or moving a user updates visibility immediately and logs to audit.

key_screens.roles_permissions: Base roles + cloned custom roles; capability toggles per module with scope (none/own/department/branch/all).
key_screens.weekly_review: Clients (new, active, at-risk, delayed), Projects (on track, delayed, blocked), Team + capacity, Finance (collections, dues, sales), Quality (complaints, revisions, QC fails), Client health (Green/Amber/Red). Every number drills down.
key_screens.pricing_engine: Edit services, tiers, deliverables, billing type, excluded notes; bundle composition with automatic 10% saving; versioned price books with effective dates; website and proposals read from active price book.
key_screens.flow_templates: Visual editor for department flows (steps, owner role, durations in working days, QC checkpoint, client review points). Templates generate tasks when a plan is approved.
key_screens.gate_rules: Read-only display of the 5 gates and their conditions; only Founder can change conditions.
key_screens.sla_rules: Response/resolution targets per request type; working-hours calendar (9:30–18:30 Mon–Sat, Sundays and government holidays off).
key_screens.impersonation: Founder/Admin may 'view as' a user for support; read-only by default, logged, client users notified.

tech_stack.web: Next.js 16 (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind 4 with BMU design tokens; route groups marketing, client, team, admin, creator, account. Light-only design. The website forwards /api/* to the API.
tech_stack.mobile: Expo SDK 57 React Native app (client + team) sharing packages/shared (types, validation, permission rules, API client); offline cache and outbox in SQLite; Expo push.
tech_stack.api: NestJS 12 modular monolith (ESM). One codebase started in three roles: PROCESS_ROLE=all (API + jobs, used by pnpm dev), api (HTTP + live updates, scale out), worker (background jobs, workflows, AI agents, webhooks). Domain events on an in-process bus shared across processes through Postgres.
tech_stack.db: PostgreSQL 16/17 + Prisma 7 (driver adapter pg). Single organisation; every query scoped by organisation and permission in the API (Postgres row-level security not used). Migrations per version in apps/api/prisma/migrations.
tech_stack.cache_queue: No Redis needed: background jobs run in the worker through one job registry (overlap protection, run history) and a Postgres advisory lock so jobs never run twice; per-person read cache in memory, cleared on every change in every process. Redis/BullMQ remain an option only if job volume demands it.
tech_stack.realtime: Server-Sent Events (/realtime) with presence; changes reach every API process through Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY (channel bmu_events).
tech_stack.storage: Uploaded files on disk under STORAGE_DIR (a Docker volume shared by API and worker); signed share links. S3/R2 + CDN still planned.
tech_stack.auth: Email OTP (phone OTP waits for an SMS/WhatsApp provider), httpOnly session cookie or bearer token, TOTP 2FA with recovery codes and passkeys (WebAuthn), session list and sign-out everywhere, 2FA enforcement per role. Google sign-in and SSO not built.
tech_stack.observability: JSON logs (LOG_FORMAT=json) with X-Request-Id on every request, /health, /health/live, /health/ready on the API and worker, process heartbeats and job history on Command Centre > System health, error log page, load test (pnpm loadtest). Sentry/PostHog/uptime monitoring not connected yet.
tech_stack.infra: Dockerfile (one image) + docker-compose.prod.yml (postgres, migrate, api, worker, web, optional forecast); pnpm build:prod + pnpm start for a server without Docker; pnpm dev with embedded Postgres for development. CI/CD, staging and point-in-time-restore backups still to set up by the hosting choice.
tech_stack.python: Optional forecasting service (services/forecast, FastAPI or standard library) used through FORECAST_URL; the API falls back to built-in TypeScript forecasts.

tech_stack_original_plan.web: Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind with design tokens; extend existing bmu-marketing repo using route groups (marketing, client, team, admin, creator)
tech_stack_original_plan.mobile: Expo React Native; shared UI package and API client
tech_stack_original_plan.api: NestJS modular monolith; module boundaries + domain events; split into services only when required
tech_stack_original_plan.db: PostgreSQL (India region) + Prisma; row-level tenant isolation
tech_stack_original_plan.storage: S3-compatible (AWS S3 Mumbai or Cloudflare R2) + CDN
tech_stack_original_plan.auth: OTP (phone/email), Google sign-in, 2FA for staff; SSO later

backend_runtime.summary: How the built backend runs as real server processes (v21). Only Postgres is required; every optional service has a built-in fallback.

processes.name: web
processes.does: Website and all web surfaces; forwards /api/* to the API

processes.name: api
processes.does: HTTP API, permissions and field access, live updates (SSE) and presence, search index
processes.instances: 1 or more behind a load balancer

processes.name: worker
processes.start: pnpm start:worker (node apps/api/dist/worker.js, PROCESS_ROLE=worker, health port 4001)
processes.does: All background jobs, workflow engine, AI agents, outgoing webhooks
processes.instances: 1 active; extra workers wait on standby (advisory lock) and take over within 15 seconds

processes.name: migrate
processes.does: Applies migrations; seeds roles, permissions, catalogue, templates, settings and the OWNER_EMAIL Founder (demo data only in development)

backend_runtime.all_in_one: PROCESS_ROLE=all (default) runs api + worker in one process for pnpm dev and small installs; a second all-in-one copy detects the jobs lock and serves the API only.

events.bus: Every database write publishes a change event (Prisma extension) and every audited action a domain event.
events.cross_process: Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY channel bmu_events; each event is sent once with the sender process id and re-published by the other processes. EVENT_BRIDGE=0 turns it off. Needs a direct connection (DIRECT_DATABASE_URL behind PgBouncer).
events.reliability: Failed listener deliveries are stored (event_failures) and retried after 1, 2, 4 and 8 minutes by the process that owns that listener, then shown on System health.

jobs.registry: apps/api/src/runtime/jobs.ts startJob(): one place that decides where jobs run, prevents overlapping runs, logs failures, records run history and drains running jobs on shutdown.
jobs.switches: AUTOMATIONS_DISABLED (all but the two people jobs), ACTIONS_JOBS_DISABLED, DELIVER_JOBS_DISABLED, AGENTS_DISABLED, WORKFLOWS_DISABLED

worker: GET :4001/health/ready (database, migrations, every job with last run and error)
health.in_app: Command Centre > System health: processes, jobs, event sharing, listeners, failed deliveries, search index, feature switches.

configuration.check: pnpm env:check, and the same check at start-up: on NODE_ENV=production the API and worker refuse to start without DATABASE_URL or with a weak JWT_SECRET, and warn about APP_URL, CORS_ORIGINS, INTEGRATIONS_KEY, SMTP and OWNER_EMAIL.
required_live: SMTP_* (or OTP_LOG=1 for the first sign-in only)

deployment.docker: cp .env.production.example .env.production; pnpm docker:up (docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file .env.production up -d --build). HTTPS reverse proxy (Caddy/Nginx) in front of port 3000. Scale: --scale api=N, keep one worker.
deployment.no_docker: pnpm install; pnpm build:prod; pnpm start (migrations, then api + worker + web with automatic restart).
deployment.updates: Pull or unzip the new version and repeat the same command; migrations run before the new API starts.
deployment.backups: pg_dump -Fc nightly plus the uploaded files folder; restore with pg_restore.
deployment.shutdown: SIGTERM/Ctrl+C: stop timers, wait for running jobs (up to 20 s), close connections, release the jobs lock.

code_layout.runtime: apps/api/src/runtime (process roles, jobs, event bridge, jobs lock, heartbeats, env check, HTTP basics), main.ts, worker.ts, health/
code_layout.platform: prisma/, platform/ (event bus, realtime, search, flags, system health), audit/, common/
code_layout.deliver: engagements/, deliver/, production/, craft/, creative/, flows/, requests/, clients/, clients-actions/

code_layout.shared: packages/shared (types, zod schemas, permission matrix, gates, catalogue, API client) used by api, web and mobile

limits: Postgres row-level security is not used; isolation is enforced in the API.
Uploaded files live on local disk; with API processes on several machines the folder must be shared storage (or move to S3/R2).
The search index and read cache are per process (kept fresh by events); each API process builds its own index on first search.
Event notifications are capped at 8 KB; very large bulk writes are shared as "several rows changed".
Phone OTP, Google sign-in, SSO, virus scanning of uploads, Sentry and PostHog are not built yet.

security_compliance: RBAC + scope check on every API call (server-side)
Encrypted credential vault; every reveal logged
DPDP Act 2023: consent, data export, deletion requests
Instant access revocation on staff offboarding
Rate limiting, file virus scan, signed URLs for files

acceptance_criteria: A client cannot see any internal note, QC result, cost or staff below CM via UI or API.
'Send to client' is impossible (UI + API) without a QC pass on that version.
Planning cannot start before RCD; RCD can only be set by the client's CM or above.
Final files cannot be downloaded by the client before final payment clears.
A request marked new direction creates an add-on that requires written client approval before tasks are created.
Every approval stores user, timestamp and version and cannot be edited.
A manager sees all records visible to their reports; moving a user in the hierarchy updates access immediately.
Catalogue price changes create a new price book version; existing proposals keep their original prices.
SLA timers pause outside 9:30–18:30 Mon–Sat and on holidays.
No feature requires a WhatsApp group; every WhatsApp alert deep-links into the app.
